**Service Name:** Spotify Terms of Use

**Key Provisions:**

* **Relationship with Spotify**: These terms govern the relationship between you, the user, and Spotify.
* **Content and License**: You give Spotify permission to use your submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, in accordance with your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Spotify processes your personal data as outlined in their published Privacy Policy. 
* **Dispute Resolution**: If a dispute arises, you'll use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either you or Spotify can terminate the agreement for the reasons outlined in the live document.
* **Contact**: For questions about these terms, refer to the company's published legal contact information.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Binding arbitration**: This means disputes will be resolved in private arbitration instead of court. Some users might find this less beneficial than going to court.
* **Class-action waiver**: This clause might make it difficult for users to join a class-action lawsuit against Spotify.

**Additional Points:**

* Spotify's AI/ML systems analyze user-submitted content, including user-uploaded audio/podcasts.
* The company uses this content for training and development purposes.
* Spotify emphasizes user settings and applicable law in handling user content.
* This version of the Terms of Service is distinct from previous versions due to the inclusion of language for AI-generated playlists and revised arbitration clauses.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SPOTIFY TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Spotify and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added language for AI-generated playlists/'AI DJ', expanded the User Content license to cover user-uploaded audio/podcasts processed by AI features, and updated arbitration and class-action waiver clauses.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Spotify to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.spotify.com/us/legal/end-user-agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.spotify.com/us/legal/end-user-agreement/ .

The Terms of Service are for Netflix. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Main Service Name:** Netflix, as described on their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* These Terms govern your relationship with Netflix and apply to all products and services provided by the company.
* **Sharing:** You need to pay for additional members in your household to use Netflix. Netflix defines a 'household' and has clearer language about this. Be aware: not all household members may be allowed to use Netflix without a separate account or payment.
* **Content Use:** Netflix can use the content you submit to operate, improve, and train their AI and machine learning systems (if allowed by your settings and the law).
* **Privacy:** Netflix's Privacy Policy explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed. Check it out for more details.
* **Disputes:** If you have a problem, Netflix requires binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out option for new accounts. If you're not sure, be sure to review the details and decide if you want out of this process.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* **Sharing Requirements:** If you have a lot of members in your household, you'll need to pay for them, as Netflix requires paid sharing for additional members.
* **AI/ML System Use:** Netflix might use your submitted content to train their AI and ML systems, which you may not agree with, depending on your preferences.
* **Termination:** Either side can terminate the agreement at any time, which could leave you without access to Netflix's services.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Binding arbitration can limit your ability to take Netflix to court, and you can only opt out within 30 days of opening an account.

To get help or more information, you can contact Netflix directly through their website.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NETFLIX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Netflix and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected the household sharing/'extra member' policy: paid sharing requires the primary household plus paid additional members, added clearer language on what constitutes a 'Netflix Household', and updated billing/cancellation provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Netflix to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse .

These Terms of Service are for the Disney+ Subscriber Agreement. Here's a summary:

**What the Service Covers**

These terms apply to your relationship with Disney+ and the products and services we offer, as listed on our website.

**Key Provisions**

* **Streaming with Ads**: Starting January 27, 2025 (for new subscribers) and March 24, 2025 (for existing ones), you may see ads on 'no ads' or 'ad-free' tiers.
* **Content and License**: We use user-generated content to improve our AI and ML systems, subject to your settings and the law.
* **User-Identifying Information**: The company's **Privacy Policy** outlines how we collect and process personal data.
* **Disputes**: We require **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with class-action waivers, except for a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can end the agreement under described conditions.
* **Contact**: For questions about these terms, see our published contact information.

**Potential User Concerns**

* **Adverts on Ad-Free tiers**: This change might be a concern for users who paid for ad-free streaming.
* **Content and AI Training**: Some users might be uneasy about their content being used without explicit consent.
* **Arbitration and Class-Action Waivers**: Users might have reservations about settling disputes privately rather than in court.
* **Limited Opt-Out Period**: The 30-day opt-out period for new accounts might be too short for users to carefully consider their options.

Overall, these terms aim to clarify the user-service relationship, but certain provisions may raise questions about user rights and data usage.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DISNEY+ SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Disney+ and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones: streaming titles may now show ads even on 'no ads'/'ad free' tiers, expanded arbitration with mass-arbitration procedures following Disney's earlier 2024 Wrongful-Death-case controversy, and updated content-availability language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Disney+ to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement .

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Multiple 2024 updates: revised seller-protection criteria, added new fee schedules for cross-border transactions, expanded the dispute resolution / chargeback flow, and clarified handling of cryptocurrency holdings. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . The previous version is available at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

**Service Name:** The eBay User Agreement

**Summary:**

The eBay User Agreement governs your relationship with eBay and is a key document for users of the platform. Here are some key points to know:

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all products and services on eBay, which you can find on the company's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you create content on eBay, you grant the company permission to use it for various purposes, like training their AI systems, subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** eBay's Privacy Policy explains the types of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most users must use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) to resolve disputes, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. [__Please note: class-action waivers mean you might not be able to join a group lawsuit.__]
* **Termination:** Either eBay or you can terminate the agreement under specific conditions.
* **Contact:** If you have questions, eBay's published legal contact information is available.

**Potential concerns:**

* **Arbitration with class-action waivers:** If you have a dispute, you might not be able to join a group lawsuit, which could limit your ability to seek compensation or changes.
* **Use of content:** While eBay has guidelines on how to use content, there's a potential risk that the company could use your data in ways you don't anticipate or agree with.

**What to be aware of:**

* Pay attention to the terms of service when you create content or lists – it's used by eBay's AI systems and may be retained and shared with third parties.
* Review the Privacy Policy to see what personal data is collected and how it's used.
* Understand that you can opt-out of arbitration within 30 days of opening a new account.
* If you're unsure about any of these terms, it's best to review the official documents or seek further clarification from eBay. 

Please keep in mind that this is a plain-English explanation of the terms, and it's essential to review the official documents for your specific needs and circumstances.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EBAY USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with eBay and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised payments-on-eBay structure for managed payments, added more detailed AI/automated-decision sections, expanded permitted-use language for listing data, and updated arbitration / opt-out procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by eBay to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 .

**Amazon Conditions of Use: A Summary**

The [Amazon Conditions of Use](https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=508088) govern your relationship with Amazon and its products and services. The Terms of Service are effective from 2024 and have undergone updates.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms apply to the products and services listed on Amazon's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** You grant Amazon permission to use your user-submitted content to improve and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration with class-action waivers, unless you opt-out within 30 days. You should note that this means that individual claims may not be represented in a group lawsuit, potentially limiting your options.
* **Privacy:** Amazon's Privacy Policy is cross-referenced for categories of personal data collected and processed.
* **Termination:** Either you or Amazon may terminate the agreement according to the conditions outlined in the Terms.

**Harmful Clauses for Users:**

* **Dispute Resolution:** As mentioned, binding arbitration with class-action waivers might restrict your ability to pursue group claims in court, potentially affecting your options for resolving disputes.
* **Termination:** Be aware that either you or Amazon can terminate the agreement under specific conditions. Review these conditions carefully to understand your obligations and triggers for termination.
* **Data Use:** While Amazon mentions using your content to improve and train its AI/ML systems, some users might be concerned about data use beyond their settings or applicable law.

**Next Steps:**

Review the original Terms of Service document to understand the full scope and any additional details that may not be covered in this summary. Be cautious when using Amazon services, particularly in regard to dispute resolution and data use.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — AMAZON CONDITIONS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Amazon and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: May 2024 update revised disputes/arbitration to explicitly permit small-claims-court actions, updated language about Amazon services covered, and added clearer references to AI features (Alexa, Rufus) and how generated content interacts with the user agreement.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Amazon to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=508088 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=508088 .

**Summary of Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions (2024)**

This document governs your relationship with Apple and applies to various Apple services, including Apple Music, iCloud, and the App Store. The Key Provisions are:

**Who and What it Applies To**

* These terms govern your relationship with Apple, which includes various products and services described on Apple's official terms page.

**How User-Submitted Content is Used**

* Apple can use your user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems.
* This usage is subject to your settings and applicable law.

**How Your Personal Data is Handled**

* Apple's Privacy Policy sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.

**Resolving Disputes**

* Most of these terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* This means you cannot take Apple to court for most disputes; instead, you'll have to go through arbitration.

**Cancellation**

* Either you or Apple can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the live document.

**Flagged Clauses that May be Harmful to the User**

* The requirement for binding arbitration with a class-action waiver (clause 5) may be concerning, as it limits your ability to take collective action against Apple in case of a dispute.
* Termination (clause 6) can be initiated by either party, so be aware that you could be denied access to Apple services without a clear reason or explanation.

**Important Contacts**

* If you have questions about these terms, see Apple's published legal contact information.

Please review these Terms of Service carefully before using Apple Media Services to understand the terms fully and feel comfortable using these services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — APPLE MEDIA SERVICES TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features, clarified content-license scope across services (iCloud, Apple Music, App Store), and revised Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html .

The service provided by these Terms of Service is called iCloud.

Here's a summary of the key provisions:

* **Scope**: These Terms apply to Apple's relationship with you and cover the products and services listed on their official terms page. This includes iCloud and possibly other Apple services.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content to Apple, they can use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems. However, this is subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: The Terms reference Apple's published Privacy Policy, which explains how they collect and process your personal data.
* **Terms and Conditions**: They can change at any time. Apple has added language about Advanced Data Protection (end-to-end encryption) and mentions of Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, as well as updated how stored content may be accessed by Apple.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most users must go through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means users give up the right to a jury trial.
* **Termination**: Either Apple or you can terminate the agreement, but the conditions are unclear.

Some potentially concerning clauses:

* **Data Sharing**: Apple may use your submitted content to train their AI/ML systems. While this is common practice, it raises concerns about data ownership and sharing.
* **Arbitration**: The requirement for binding arbitration can be unforgiving if users disagree with Apple. It's essential to understand that users may face restrictions when trying to pursue disputes in court.
* **Termination**: The lack of clarity in the termination conditions raises questions about what protections, if any, are in place for users.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ICLOUD TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Advanced Data Protection (end-to-end encryption) language, references to Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, and revised provisions about how stored content may be accessed by Apple for legal/safety reasons.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html .

Let's break down these Terms of Service for you.

**Service Name:** Snap (Snapchat) Terms of Service.

**Key Provisions:**

### Scope

These Terms of Service apply to all products and services offered by Snap (Snapchat).

### Content and License

When you submit content to Snap (such as images, videos, or text), you grant the company permission to use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems. However, the company must follow your settings and applicable law.

### Privacy

The company's Privacy Policy determines what personal data is collected and how it's handled. This Policy is separate from the Terms of Service.

### Dispute Resolution

Most of these Terms require _binding arbitration_ (a private dispute process instead of court) with _class-action waivers_ (this means you can't join a group lawsuit against Snap). However, you have 30 days after creating a new account to opt out of this requirement.

### Termination

Either you or Snap can terminate the agreement at any time, but the Terms describe specific conditions for this to happen.

**Red Flags:**

* **Class-action waivers:** These _restrict your right to participate in group lawsuits_ against Snap. If another user has a legitimate case, you might be limited in how you can address it.
* **Binding arbitration:** This _replaces court proceedings_, which might not provide the same protections as a public trial.
* **Limited termination conditions:** Although either party can terminate the agreement, the Terms might not specify how this works in practice, which could lead to difficulties.
* **Data collection and usage:** The Company's Privacy Policy might not fully detail how it handles personal data. Be sure to read it carefully.

Please be aware that this summary is based on the provided Terms of Service, but if you have specific questions or concerns, I recommend reading the full document and exploring Snap's (Snapchat) published policies.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SNAP TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Snap (Snapchat) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective April 7, 2025: added new sections on My AI and other generative-AI features, expanded the user-content license for Live/Local/crowd-sourced services, clarified data-sharing with parents (for under-18 users via Family Center), and updated arbitration pre-dispute notice procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Snap (Snapchat) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.snap.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.snap.com/terms .

The Terms of Service outline the agreement between you and Pinterest, the social media platform for sharing and discovering visual content.

**Service Name**: The Terms of Service apply to the products and services described on Pinterest's official terms page, which govern your relationship with the company.

**Key Provisions**:

* **Content and License**: You grant Pinterest permission to use your submitted content to operate, improve, and train their Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. This means that Pinterest can use your content to create better recommendations, but they are required to respect your settings and follow the law.
* **Privacy**: The Terms cross-reference Pinterest's published Privacy Policy, which explains what data they collect from you and how they process it.
* **Dispute Resolution**: The Terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. This means that if you have a dispute with Pinterest, you won't be able to join a group lawsuit or ask a court to make a decision for your case.
* **Termination**: Either you or Pinterest can terminate the agreement, but you'll need to follow the conditions described in the live document.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user**:

* The requirement for binding arbitration (Dispute Resolution) means you won't have the option to resolve disputes through a court or participate in a group lawsuit.
* The Terms give Pinterest permission to use your content to train their AI/ML systems without providing explicit opt-in for this use. However, this is subject to your settings and applicable law, so be sure to review Pinterest's content use policies.
* If you have a dispute with Pinterest, you'll need to opt-out within 30 days of opening a new account to avoid the arbitration requirement.

Overall, the Terms of Service outline the basics of your agreement with Pinterest, including how they can use your content, your privacy expectations, and how disputes will be resolved.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PINTEREST TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Pinterest and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added language permitting Pinterest to use public Pin content to train AI/ML models for recommendations and safety, clarified obligations for advertisers and merchants, and updated arbitration provisions. Pinterest publishes a public archive at policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Pinterest to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive .

**What Tumblr can do with your content:**

Tumblr uses your submitted content to operate and improve their services, including training their AI and machine learning systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.

**User data and privacy:**

The Terms of Service cross-reference Tumblr's published Privacy Policy, which explains how they collect and process your personal data.

**How to resolve disputes:**

In the case of disagreements, you and Tumblr will engage in binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers, unless you opt out of arbitration within 30 days of creating your account. Note that some users might find this clause concerning as it limits your ability to join a class-action lawsuit.

**Terminating the agreement:**

Either party can terminate the agreement, but the Terms of Service don't provide a clear explanation of what "conditions" this is subject to.

**Getting in touch with Tumblr:**

If you have questions or concerns about these Terms, you can visit Tumblr's website at https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service for their contact information.

Flagged clauses that may be harmful to the user: 

* The binding arbitration clause with class-action waivers may limit your ability to join a class-action lawsuit and resolve disputes in a fair and public way.
* The lack of clear conditions for termination may leave users uncertain about their rights and responsibilities.
* The use of public content for AI training, while optional, may not be explicit enough to avoid accidental data sharing. 

These Terms of Service aim to clearly outline Tumblr's use of user-submitted content, data collection, and dispute resolution processes. However, users should be aware of the clauses that may have a negative impact on their rights or experiences.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TUMBLR TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Tumblr and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected Automattic's deal to share public Tumblr posts with AI partners (e.g. for training): added language confirming use of public content for AI training and added a user-facing opt-out (Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Tumblr to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service .

**Service Name:** Dropbox Terms of Service (2024 version)

**Summary:** These Terms of Service outline the rules and regulations for using Dropbox and its features. They aim to ensure a smooth, protected, and beneficial experience for users while protecting Dropbox's rights and interests. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

### 1. Scope

The terms apply to all Dropbox products and services mentioned on the official terms page.

### 2. Content and License

When you submit content to Dropbox, it may be used to:

* Operate and improve Dropbox's services
* Train AI and Machine Learning (ML) systems (but only with your consent)
subject to your settings and applicable law

### 3. Privacy

Dropbox's Privacy Policy (cross-referenced in the terms) explains how your personal data is collected and processed. (Please note that the actual Privacy Policy is not included in these Terms of Service.)

### 4. Dispute Resolution

In case of disputes, most terms require **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of court). This means you'll give up your right to a jury trial and join a class-action lawsuit. However, new accounts have a 30-day opt-out window, allowing you to avoid this requirement.

**Harmful Clause:** The mandatory arbitration process may limit your access to court and reduce your options for resolving disputes.

### 5. Termination

Either you or Dropbox can terminate the agreement, but termination conditions are not explicitly stated in these Terms of Service.

### 6. Contact

For questions about these terms, refer to Dropbox's published legal contact information at the provided URL.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* Lack of explicit termination conditions may lead to misunderstandings or disputes.
* The mandatory arbitration requirement, although opt-outable for new accounts, may still be problematic for users who don't opt out timely.

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Dropbox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Late-2023/early-2024 update added Dropbox AI features (Dropbox Dash, AI search/summary). After user backlash, Dropbox amended language (Dec 2023 / 2024) to explicitly state customer data is not used to train third-party AI models without consent.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Dropbox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.dropbox.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230601000000*/https://www.dropbox.com/terms .

**Service Name:** Canva Terms of Use

**Summary:** These Terms of Service outline the guidelines for using Canva's products and services. The main terms govern how user-submitted content is used, handled, and protected.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms apply to all Canva products and services listed on the company's official terms page.
* **Content and License**: If you submit content to Canva, the company has the right to use it to operate, improve, and train their AI systems. This is subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy**: Canva's Privacy Policy explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed. This document cross-references that policy.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes must go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers (you can't join a group lawsuit). You have 30 days to opt-out of this arbitration clause when creating a new account.
* **Termination**: Either party can cancel the agreement according to conditions in the document.
* **Contact**: If you have questions, see Canva's legal contact information at their Terms of Use URL.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Arbitration With Class-Action Waivers**: This clause may limit your access to justice if you're affected by a wider issue. You should carefully consider the 30-day opt-out window when creating a new account.
* **Content Moderation Requirements**: The updated terms require content-moderation/labeling for Canva-generated content, which might raise questions about data accuracy and retention.

**Note:** If you're concerned about any specific aspects of these Terms of Service, review them carefully or consult an attorney. These explanations aim to clarify what the document says, not provide professional advice.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — CANVA TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Canva and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Canva's generative AI tools (Magic Studio): users own outputs subject to platform rights, restrictions on using Canva-generated content to train other AI models, and new content-moderation/labeling requirements.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Canva to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ .

The Terms of Service are for Notion, a product and service offered by Notion. 

These terms explain how using Notion will affect your relationship with the company and spell out the agreements between you and Notion. The main provisions include:

* **Content and License**: Any content you submit to Notion can be used to make the service work, improve it, and train Notion's AI/ML systems. This depends on your settings and the laws in your area.
* **Privacy**: The terms of service reference Notion's [Privacy Policy](url), which describes the types of personal data gathered and how it is treated.
* **Dispute Resolution**: In case of disagreements, most terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). This typically means you cannot join a class-action lawsuit. You have 30 days after signing up to opt out (except for users like Steam/Valve).
* **Termination**: Either you or Notion may end the agreement according to the details in the document.

There are also some key points to consider:

* **Changes to the Terms**: Notion has the right to update the Terms of Service and modify their service offerings or features, without your permission.
* **Responsible use**: By using Notion, you agree to use the service in a way that complies with the laws and community guidelines. If you are unsure what that is, review Notion's documentation.
 
Please note that the clauses that may be disadvantageous to users are:

* Mandatory binding arbitration for disputes (except for Steam/Valve accounts), which removes your ability to partake in class-action lawsuits.
* You can't use your data (content, not personal identifiable information) to train Notion's foundational AI models, unless you opt-in.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NOTION TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Notion and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Notion AI provisions (input/output ownership, no training of foundational models on customer data by default), updated subprocessor list, and clarified data-residency options for enterprise plans.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Notion to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.notion.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.notion.so/terms .

**Service Name:** Figma Terms of Service

**Summary:** These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Figma, the online platform for creating, designing, and collaborating on digital projects. The document covers the use of Figma's products and services, how you can contribute to them, and what you can expect from Figma in return.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms of Service apply to all Figma products and services listed on the official terms page.
* **Content and License:** You agree to let Figma use your submitted content (like designs, files, etc.) to improve and train their AI/ML systems. This will happen in accordance with your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Figma cross-references their published Privacy Policy to explain what data is collected and how it's processed. You should read the Privacy Policy to understand how your data is used.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most clauses require **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of court) with **class-action waivers**. This means you can't file a lawsuit or join a group lawsuit against Figma.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under the terms described in the document.
* **Contact:** For questions about the Terms of Service, visit the published legal contact information at the Figma website.

**Clauses to Consider Carefully:**

* The requirement for **binding arbitration** with **class-action waivers** might limit your ability to seek compensation or justice in a group or in a court of law.
* The use of your submitted content to **train AI/ML systems** might be concerning if you're not comfortable with this. However, the Terms of Service do mention your settings and applicable law, which may help mitigate concerns.

Please note that these Terms of Service are subject to change, and this summary might not be comprehensive or up-to-date. Always refer to the official document for the latest information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FIGMA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Figma and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Figma AI features (Make Designs, Visual Search) provisions, clarified that customer file content is not used to train third-party generative models without opt-in, and updated security and incident-notification language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Figma to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.figma.com/legal/tos/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.figma.com/tos/ .

The service is the Stack Overflow Public Network, which is governed by these updated Terms of Service, effective 2024.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to the Stack Overflow products and services described on the company's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Stack Overflow, you license it under CC BY-SA (a Creative Commons license that allows others to share and adapt the material, as long as they give proper credit).
	+ **Note:** There's a restriction on bulk extraction of content for training AI systems without a commercial agreement. This means that if you want to use Stack Overflow content for training AI, you'll need to get a special deal with the company.
* **Privacy:** The terms reference Stack Overflow's published Privacy Policy, which explains how personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If you have a dispute with Stack Overflow, the terms require that you go through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either you or Stack Overflow can terminate the agreement under certain conditions.
* **Contact:** If you have questions about these terms, you can find Stack Overflow's contact information at the new TOS URL.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Arbitration Clause:** Requiring binding arbitration with a class-action waiver may limit your ability to bring a class-action lawsuit or join one with other users.
	+ **Note:** This clause has been criticized by some for favoring companies over individual users.
* **Restrictions on AI Training Data:** The restriction on bulk extraction of content for AI training without a commercial agreement may limit users' ability to use Stack Overflow content for non-commercial purposes.

Keep in mind that these concerns are a plain-language interpretation of the terms and may not necessarily be a comprehensive analysis of their implications.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STACK OVERFLOW PUBLIC NETWORK TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Stack Overflow and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: May 2024 update added a 'Generative AI / LLM' restriction explicitly licensing posted Q&A under CC BY-SA but limiting bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, after the company's content-licensing deals with OpenAI and Google.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Stack Overflow to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public .

**Service Name:** Quora Terms of Service

These Terms of Service outline the rules and agreements between you (as a user) and Quora. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope:**
These terms apply to all Quora products and services listed on the company's official terms page.

**Content and License:**
When you submit content on Quora, you're granting the company permission to use it to improve and develop their AI and machine learning systems. How your content is used depends on your settings and applicable laws.

**Privacy:**
Quora's Privacy Policy explains how your personal data is collected and processed. The Privacy Policy is separate from these Terms of Service, but it's referenced here as a cross-reference.

**Dispute Resolution:**
The updated terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) for disputes, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means that if you have a disagreement with Quora, you'll need to use a private arbitration process to resolve it, rather than going to court. Some classes of users (e.g., those who are employees of other companies) may be waived from this requirement.

**Termination:**
Either Quora or you can terminate the agreement under the conditions described in the live document.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Notice:** The update adds rules for Quora's AI chatbot platform, Poe, and requires users to agree to terms for interacting with Poe. Users' prompts and responses may be used to improve Poe and partner models, subject to their settings.
* **Opt-out:** New users have a 30-day window to opt out of binding arbitration.
* **Termination:** The agreement can be terminated under specified conditions.
* **Additional terms:** Bot-developer terms are added for users who interact with the Poe platform.

**Potential Red Flags:**

* **Data usage:** Users may be concerned about how Quora uses their content and data, especially in regards to improving AI and machine learning systems.
* **Dispute resolution:** The requirement for binding arbitration may be seen as negative by users who prefer to resolve disputes in court.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — QUORA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Quora and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Poe (Quora's AI chatbot platform): user prompts/responses may be used to improve Poe and partner models subject to settings, added bot-developer terms, and revised dispute resolution.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Quora to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.quora.com/about/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.quora.com/about/tos .

response:
**Service Name:** 23andMe Terms of Service

**Key Provisions:**

* The Terms of Service govern your relationship with 23andMe, which includes its products and services (listed on the company's official terms page).
* You agree to arbitrate (resolve) disputes with 23andMe, rather than going to court. To avoid this, you must opt-out within 30 days of creating an account. (This means you'll give up your right to sue in court and participate in class-action lawsuits.)
* You retain ownership of any content you submit to 23andMe, but the company may use it to improve its AI/ML systems.
* The company collects personal data, as outlined in its published Privacy Policy.
* Either party may terminate the agreement under certain conditions (found in the live document).

**Harmful Clauses to User:**

* **Arbitration clause with class-action waiver:** This means you may not join a class-action lawsuit or sue in court if you have a dispute with 23andMe. You'll be required to go to binding arbitration, even if more than one person was affected by a problem.
* **30-day opt-out window:** If you don't opt-out of arbitration within 30 days of creating an account, you'll be bound by this clause. If you're not aware of this requirement, you may unintentionally waive your right to sue.
* **Mandatory arbitration:** If you have a problem with 23andMe and don't opt-out, you'll be required to use a private dispute resolution process (binding arbitration) instead of going to court.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

**Service Name:** These Terms of Service govern the relationship between Twitch and its users, covering the products and services listed on its official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Twitch, they use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems. This means that Twitch might use your videos, clips, or other content to improve their services, but only if you allow them to do so according to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Twitch collects personal data, and its Privacy Policy explains what categories of data are collected and how it is processed. We recommend checking the Privacy Policy for details.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes will need to go through **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means that you or Twitch can opt out of this process within 30 days of creating your Twitch account, but after that, you will be bound by this process. We flag this as a potentially **harmful clause**, as it may limit your ability to take disputes to court.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under the conditions described in the live document.

**Other Points to Consider:**

* **New Branded Content Disclosure Rules:** In 2024, Twitch introduced new rules for disclosing branded content, which might affect users who create sponsored content.
* **Termination of the Agreement:** The agreement can be terminated under the conditions described in the live document.

**Harmful Clauses to User:**

* The **binding arbitration** clause, which may limit your ability to take disputes to court.

Please note that it's essential to check the **Privacy Policy** for more details about what data is collected and how it is processed.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TWITCH TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Twitch and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added new Branded Content disclosure rules, expanded the User Content license to support clips, replays and AI-generated highlights, and updated the dispute-resolution mass-arbitration procedure.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Twitch to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ .

**Service Name:** Roblox Terms of Use (effective 2024)

**Summary:** These Terms govern your relationship with Roblox, a platform where users create and play games. The Terms outline how Roblox uses your content, handles disputes, and terminates accounts.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** The Terms apply to Roblox's products and services, as listed on the official Terms page.
* **Content and License:** You grant Roblox a license to use your submitted content for various purposes (operating, improving, training AI/ML systems). However, your settings and applicable law apply if you're under 13 (minor-protection clause).
* **Dispute Resolution:** If a dispute arises, most cases require you to participate in binding arbitration, which skips the courts and often includes a class-action waiver (except for Valve/Steam accounts). You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts to avoid this.
* **Termination:** Roblox or you can terminate the agreement, subject to conditions in the live document.
* **Contact:** Questions or concerns about the Terms should be directed to Roblox's published legal contact information.

**Clauses that may be harmful to users:**

* **Section 5 (Dispute Resolution):** Arbitration means disputes are settled privately instead of in court. A class-action waiver may limit your ability to group similar cases in a single lawsuit. *However, note that this does not apply to Valve/Steam accounts.*
* **Section 3 (Content and License):** Granting a license for AI/ML system training might make you uncomfortable, especially if you're under 13.
* **Section 6 (Termination):** Losing access to your account or data can be frustrating. Be sure to understand the conditions for termination before submitting data.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ROBLOX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Roblox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update strengthened minor-protection language (default-private accounts under 13, parental-consent flows), updated Robux/DevEx provisions, added rules for Roblox's generative-AI 'Studio Assistant' and avatar-creation tools, and revised arbitration class-waiver section.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Roblox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.

**Service Name:** Steam Subscriber Agreement

**Summary:** These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Steam (a service provided by Valve) when using their products and services. Here's what you need to know:

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all Steam products and services, as described on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you create and share content on Steam, the company uses it to improve their services, subject to your account settings and local laws.
* **Privacy:** Your personal data is protected under Steam's published **Privacy Policy**, which lists what data is collected and how it's used. (We'll discuss harm flags below.)
* **Termination:** You or Steam can terminate this agreement, but there are conditions described in the live document.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most users must use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. However, Steam has now removed mandatory arbitration, allowing users to file disputes in court (subject to venue rules).

**Harm Flags:**

* **Class-action waivers:** This means you might not have the right to join a group lawsuit with other users who've been affected by the same issue.
* **Binding arbitration:** You'll have to go through a private dispute process instead of court, which might limit your options for resolving disputes.
* **Personal data collection:** While Steam's Privacy Policy sets out what data is collected, the fact that it's shared with third parties (for AI/ML training, for example) raises concerns about data security and misuse.

**Important Contacts:**

* For questions about these terms, check Steam's published legal contact information at their TOS URL: https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/
* The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STEAM SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Steam (Valve) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: September 26, 2024 update removed the mandatory arbitration / class-action waiver clauses entirely - Valve now requires disputes to be filed in court (subject to venue rules), reversing several years of arbitration-only language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Steam (Valve) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ .

These Terms of Service apply to Epic Games' products and services, which include popular games like Fortnite. The main points to know are:

* **Scope**: The Terms of Service govern your relationship with Epic Games and cover their various products and services.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content to Epic Games, they can use it to improve their services, train their AI, or operate their systems, depending on your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy**: Your personal data is collected under Epic Games' Privacy Policy, which explains how your data is processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: You agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) if an issue arises. This means you can't participate in a class-action lawsuit and may have a limited window (30 days for new accounts) to opt out.
* **Termination**: Either party can end the agreement with certain conditions.
* **Contact**: For questions or concerns, you can find Epic Games' legal contact information on their website.

Key provisions that may be notable to users:

* **User-Generated Content (UGC)**: When you submit UGC, Epic Games may use it in various ways, including training AI/ML systems. You should review the settings and applicable laws to understand what happens to your content.
* **Dispute Resolution**: The binding arbitration clause means you may have limited options for resolving disputes with Epic Games. While this reduces the cost and time associated with resolving disputes, it also restricts your ability to participate in a class-action lawsuit.
* **Termination**: Epic Games can end the agreement with certain conditions. Be aware that this provision may allow them to terminate your account or services with minimal notice.

Overall, these Terms of Service aim to govern your relationship with Epic Games and their various products and services. By understanding these key provisions, you can be more informed about your interactions with the company.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EPIC GAMES TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Epic Games and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised the Fortnite/Epic Account language, added User-Generated Content (UEFN) provisions and creator-payout rules, updated EU-specific consumer-rights language post-DMA, and refreshed dispute-resolution sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Epic Games to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos .

**Service Name:** DoorDash Consumer Terms of Service

These terms govern your use of various DoorDash products and services, which include things like ordering food for delivery.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to the services listed on DoorDash's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** You agree to allow DoorDash to use any content you submit (like ratings or reviews), but only in accordance with your account settings and applicable law. DoorDash will use this content to operate and improve its services.
* **Privacy:** Your personal data is collected and processed according to DoorDash's separate Privacy Policy, which lists the types of data it collects.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If there's a dispute, you and DoorDash agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means you can't join a group lawsuit against DoorDash if there's a class-action dispute.
* **Termination:** Either you or DoorDash can terminate the agreement based on the conditions described in the live document.

**Potential Red Flags for Users:**

* **Arbitration Clause:** You're required to go to private arbitration instead of court, unless you opt-out within 30 days of creating an account. This might make it harder to take action against DoorDash in certain situations.
* **Data Use:** DoorDash collects and processes your personal data, but the specific provisions for using user-submitted content might be concerning for some users.
* **Termination:** It's usually a good idea to understand the conditions under which your account can be terminated. If there are specific grounds or notice requirements, they're likely described in the live document.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DOORDASH CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with DoorDash and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised arbitration provisions (including mass-arbitration handling), added DashPass auto-renewal clarifications, updated tipping/refund mechanics and added new sections covering AI-generated menu summaries and order-suggestion features.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by DoorDash to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service .
